# positional index path caveat
Source: https://llms-explorer.com/tree/positional-index-path-caveat/

# positional index path caveat — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for positional index path caveat. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Structure and components

- [statement] A 2019 demonstration creates {"parts.0.sku":1} and obtains FETCH over IXSCAN for {"parts.0.sku":"abc"}. Its scalar-at-that-position example reports isMultiKey:false. Treat this as a demonstrated schema-specific option, not a guarantee that every positional index is non-multikey. (low confidence) — https://www.plusnconsulting.com/post/Positional-Array-Indexing-in-MongoDB/index.html
- [statement] The +N example reports isMultiKey:false for its scalar first-element sku path. Treat this as a property of that demonstrated schema; the article does not establish that every path containing a numeric component is necessarily non-multikey. (low confidence) — https://www.plusnconsulting.com/post/Positional-Array-Indexing-in-MongoDB/index.html
- [statement] Wildcard indexes omit array positions, but this does not prohibit all positional predicates: MongoDB documents ship.captains.0.name as eligible, and its planner matches some paths with numeric components removed when the parent is multikey. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/embedded-object-behavior.md · keywords: positional index path caveat · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/query/planner_wildcard_helpers.cpp
- [statement] Numeric dotted components can mean field names as well as positions. SERVER-27442 demonstrates that {"a.2":99} matches both {"a":[1,32,99]} and {"a":[{"2":99},1,2]}; wildcard planner code explicitly enumerates field-name and array-index interpretations. Avoid assuming positional syntax alone disambiguates heterogeneous arrays. (high confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-27442?attachmentOrder=desc · keywords: positional index path caveat · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/query/planner_wildcard_helpers.cpp

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] An index restricted to parts.0.sku cannot stand in for an index supporting the any-element predicate parts.sku: the 2019 demonstration shows COLLSCAN for that broader predicate because the positional index omits other elements. (low confidence) — https://www.plusnconsulting.com/post/Positional-Array-Indexing-in-MongoDB/index.html
- [statement] A wildcard index cannot support ship.coordinates.0.1 when coordinates contains arrays directly inside an array: it stores each inner array as a whole. The planner also rejects adjacent positional components following a multikey component because they may require matching inside a nested array. Another eligible index may still serve the query. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/embedded-object-behavior.md · keywords: positional index path caveat · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/query/planner_wildcard_helpers.cpp
- [statement] The inspected wildcard planner rejects a query path included through an array-index wildcard projection: for multikey a, projection {"a.0":1} treats 0 as a field name and cannot safely supply {"a.0.b":...} under array-position query semantics. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/query/planner_wildcard_helpers.cpp

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Wildcard query eligibility is limited to at most eight explicit array indices in a field path; this is not an eight-level document-indexing depth limit. Planner comments explain that numeric field-name versus array-index interpretations require exponential path enumeration. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/embedded-object-behavior.md · keywords: positional index path caveat · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/query/planner_wildcard_helpers.cpp
- [statement] For a fixed-position workload, validate the exact predicate with explain and inspect bounds and document examination, rather than accepting IXSCAN alone. This recommendation follows the targeted positional-index demonstration and the historical full-range hinted-index counterexample. (medium confidence) — https://www.plusnconsulting.com/post/Positional-Array-Indexing-in-MongoDB/index.html · keywords: positional index path caveat · also: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/30469564/mongodb-not-using-multikey-index

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Do not assume an index on array supplies useful bounds for array.2. Independent user examples report that an ordinary multikey index loses position information; a MongoDB 3.0.3 reproduction shows an unhinted COLLSCAN and a hinted IXSCAN with full [MinKey, MaxKey] bounds. These are historical demonstrations, not benchmarks for current releases. (high confidence) — https://stackoverflow.com/questions/49134851/indexing-mongodb-array-position-queries · keywords: positional index path caveat · also: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/30469564/mongodb-not-using-multikey-index, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md
- [statement] SERVER-119604 reports different results for {"A.0.B":{$ne:null}} before and after index creation and after inserting an empty array on MongoDB 8.0.19. The ticket was resolved Works as Designed on March 19, 2026; this is a reported version-specific reproduction, not an independently reproduced universal index bug. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-19) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-119604
- [statement] In section 8.4, UC Berkeley researchers distinguish any-element queries from fixed-position queries in Arx, maintaining a separate names.0 index for the latter. Their prototype targets MongoDB 3.0; this corroborates the conceptual distinction but does not establish current MongoDB planner behavior. (low confidence) — https://iot.stanford.edu/pubs/arx-preprint.pdf
